history.dynasty: Kakatiya (present temple associated with the Kakatiya period; a 1199 CE Kakatiya-era inscription from Manthani, reign of Ganapati, is documented)
history.period: 12th-13th century Kakatiya (temple); town's Vedic tradition older - treat precisely dated claims cautiously
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is at Manthani town, Manthani mandal, Peddapalli district (not Ramagundam - about 27-33 km away). Well-supported identity. Manthani (traditionally Mantrakuta/Mantrakootam, 'Dakshina Kashi') is an ancient centre of Vedic learning on the southern bank of the Godavari; its presiding deity is Gautameswara, a form of Shiva established per tradition by Rishi Gautama. The present temple is associated with the Kakatiya period; architecture and sculpture are compared with the Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda. A 1199 CE Kakatiya inscription from Manthani records a land transaction by a priest connected with the king, giving firm epigraphic backing to the Kakatiya-era religious activity. Features: large black-stone Shivalingam (~1.25 m) on carved panavattika with somasutra; large carved Nandi at the entrance (its nose and ears damaged in periods of conflict per local tradition); Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra teerthams within the complex; other historic shrines nearby (Lakshmi Narayana, Saileshwara, Mahalakshmi, Saraswati, Panchayatanam). A later tradition associates Adi Shankara with a visit to Mantrakootam - retain as traditional account, not established history. Opening hours not published; confirm locally.

name: Manthani Gauthameswara Temple
town: Manthani (CSV town 'Ramagundam' is WRONG - the temple is at Manthani town, Manthani mandal, Peddapalli district, about 27-33 km from Ramagundam)
town_description: Manthani is a heritage town in Peddapalli district on the southern bank of the Godavari, traditionally identified with Mantrakuta/Mantrakootam and known as Dakshina Kashi. Documented as an ancient centre of Vedic learning, it holds a cluster of historic Shiva, Vishnu and goddess shrines amid a Godavari landscape with reserve forest to the east and Ravula Cheruvu lake to the west. About 33 km by road from Ramagundam railway station, 69-70 km from Karimnagar, and about 232 km from Hyderabad by road.

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad - about 232 km by road.
travel.railway: Manthani has no railway station; Ramagundam station is about 33 km by road, Peddapalli Junction also nearby.
travel.road: Connected by TSRTC buses (Manthani depot) to Karimnagar, Hyderabad, Godavarikhani, Warangal, Mancherial.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for comfortable heritage exploration; Maha Shivaratri for the festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Hours vary; no published timings found - confirm locally before a dedicated visit (verify). Entry normally free (no standard monument fee); special puja arrangements to be confirmed.
